## Build CLI binding using CMake

### Prerequisites

- [Android NDK](https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides/cmake)
- [CMake](https://cmake.org/)

### Build

```bash
# Build the CLI tool
cmake -B build-android -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-28 -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$ANDROID_NDK_HOME/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake
cmake --build build-android --parallel --config Release
```

Based on the provided documentation, here is a structured summary and guide for using **llama.cpp** with **Ascend NPU** (CANN backend).

### 1. Overview
This backend integrates llama.cpp with Huawei's Ascend NPU using the CANN Toolkit. It supports both inference and training kernels via Ascend NPU directly.

### 2. System Requirements

#### Operating System
*   **Linux** (Verified on Ubuntu 22.04 and OpenEuler 22.03).

#### Hardware (Ascend NPU)
You can identify your device ID using:
```sh
lspci -n | grep -Eo '19e5:d[0-9a-f]{3}' | cut -d: -f2
```

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

### CUDA Graphs

llama.cpp supports CUDA graphs for faster inference. To enable it, use the `--cuda-graphs` flag.

### CUDA Memory Pool

llama.cpp supports CUDA memory pool for faster memory allocation. To enable it, use the `--cuda-mempool` flag.

### CUDA Memory Alignment

llama.cpp supports CUDA memory alignment for faster memory allocation. To enable it, use the `--cuda-mem-align` flag.

### CUDA Async

llama.cpp supports CUDA async for faster memory allocation. To enable it, use the `--cuda-async` flag.

### CUDA Fallback

llama.cpp supports CUDA fallback for faster memory allocation. To enable it, use the `--cuda-fallback` flag.

### CUDA Stream

llama.cpp supports CUDA stream for faster memory allocation. To enable it, use the `--cuda-stream` flag.

### CUDA Graphs with Split Layers

llama.cpp supports CUDA graphs with split layers for faster inference. To enable it, use the `--cuda-graphs` flag.

To check if this is the case, you can use the `htop` command to monitor CPU usage. If you see CPU usage at 100%, then you should reduce the number of threads.

## Verifying that the GPU is not oversaturated
llama accepts a `-ngl N` (or `--n-gpu-layers N`) flag to configure the number of layers to offload to the GPU. If you set this to a very large number, the GPU will be oversaturated, and inference will be slower. To check if this is the case, you can use the `nvidia-smi` command to monitor GPU usage. If you see GPU usage at 100%, then you should reduce the number of layers.
